title: Handshake handoff assertions and snapshot retention for sticky oncall ownership
author: Priya Singh
description: Motivation: handoffs are a frequent source of incident friction when telemetry context is lost or ownership is ambiguous. This PR introduces a lightweight handshake/assertion protocol plus a short-term snapshot persistence layer so the outgoing oncall can assert intent (sticky ownership) and ensure the next responder receives a deterministic snapshot of relevant telemetry. Design: 1) Handoff assertions: a new handoff API that records an assertion object (owner, intent, TTL, safe-rollback hints, topical tags) to the oncall metadata store. Assertions are signed by the oncall's service identity to avoid accidental overrides. 2) Snapshot preserver: capture a compact telemetry bundle (traces, top-5 recent logs, sampled spans, alert deltas, feature flag state) into an immutable, encrypted snapshot referenced by the assertion. Snapshots are small by default (<250KB) with configurable included artifacts. 3) Read-after-handoff semantics: the receiving oncall client reads the assertion and snapshot atomically and gets a suggested checklist and sensitivity mask. 4) Safety: PII redaction and retention policy (default 72 hours) with automatic garbage collection and audit logging. 5) Feature gating and opt-out: organizations can disable persistent snapshots or reduce retention via config. Rollout: feature-gated behind slo-toolkit.handoff_handshake flag, staged rollout to 10% of teams for 2 weeks before org-wide roll. Backwards compatibility: clients that do not understand assertions ignore them; no blocking changes to runbooks. Checklist: - [x] proto and API surface defined - [x] snapshot serializer + encryption hook implemented - [x] oncall-cli integration for send/receive - [x] unit + integration tests (incl. GC) - [x] docs + migration notes - [x] privacy review and retention defaults Commit summary and code touches: see commits. Testing: CI passed after a flaky telemetry-parser test was retried; added integration test that simulates a handoff and verifies snapshot integrity across process restart. Migration notes: existing handoff flow is untouched; when enabled, outgoing oncall will attach an assertion automatically during manual handoffs and during incident archive transitions. Linear/Jira: implements ENG-3245 (handoff UX) and ENG-3290 (telemetry snapshot plumbing).

notes_for_ops: Feature is feature-gated. To enable for a team set slo-toolkit.handoff_handshake=true in org config. Monitor GC job and snapshot-store S3 usage. Run 'slo-toolkit migrate handoff-assertions' to prepopulate tenants if desired.
